Jeremy Trump's R1 annual summary gives a single whole-river trip total per species-year (boat/shore split, no guided/unguided, no per-CRC-area breakdown - crc_area is NA in district_creel_summary.csv). Combined here across all six Snake R. System CRC areas so P2 does not also try to ratio-expand them individually and double-count against this real total. Per Jeremy (2026-08-20): the creel covers specific open zones, not whole CRC areas - spring Chinook covers a portion of 640 and 644, fall Chinook a portion of 644 and 648; areas 642, 646, 650 have no creel presence in either season. Confirmed clean, not a mismatch: the creel covers all open water completely, and harvest can only occur where fishing is legally open, so CRC harvest for 640/644 (spring) or 644/648 (fall) reflects the same water the creel covers - closed portions of the CRC area produce no harvest to miss. The remaining limitation is narrower than a spatial gap: Jeremy's total is one combined number per season across whichever areas were open that season (640+644 for spring, 644+648 for fall), not split area-by-area, so a season-specific trips/CRC-harvest ratio using the matching combined area harvest is a clean quantity in principle - not yet computed as a real ColumbiaSnake donor pair, still covered_unpartitioned/columbia_pooled pending that build. 642/646/650 remain genuinely uncovered by any creel, in any season.
